differential.name: Acute ST‑segment elevation myocardial infarction
differential.rationale: Known recent STEMI in a 57‑year‑old with hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia and prior MI makes this the most likely cause of current symptoms.

differential.name: Unstable angina / non‑ST‑segment elevation myocardial infarction
differential.rationale: Similar risk profile; could present with chest discomfort without full ST‑elevation.

differential.name: Aortic dissection (type B)
differential.rationale: Severe hypertension and acute chest/back pain in a middle‑aged male; life‑threatening but less common than coronary events.

differential.name: Pulmonary embolism
differential.rationale: Risk factors include immobility from chronic pain and possible hypercoagulability (elevated platelets); can mimic chest pain and dyspnea.

differential.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
differential.rationale: Common cause of retrosternal discomfort; considered after more serious cardiac/vascular etiologies are excluded.
